why: The answer gives no output for any of the three inputs. Its only claim is that StdIn is a variable holding all the numbers like an array, and that contradicts Java: StdIn is a library that reads tokens one at a time from an input stream, and each read uses up its token.

concepts.quote: StdIn is a variable that holds all the numbers, like an array.
concepts.why: It treats StdIn as stored data you can look at, not a stream where each readInt() takes the next token.

concepts.quote: a variable that holds all the numbers
concepts.why: It says one variable can hold many values, which matches the MultiValueVariable misconception.
The answer says nothing about the loop or isEmpty().

concepts.quote: holds all the numbers, like an array
concepts.why: It reads the input as a list stored in place that can be revisited, not a stream whose values are used up as they are read.
